'''Tai Shrine''' (たいじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Seki, Gifu|Q860647|qid=Q860647}}, {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|Q131277|qid=Q131277}}. It is a shrine listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki}} for Kamo District, {{ill|Mino Province|Q864156|qid=Q864156}}, and its former rank was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

=== History ===
The date of foundation is unknown. In the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'', it is listed as a small state-supported shrine; in the ''{{ill|Izumi Province Divine Name Register|Q11420490|qid=Q11420490}}'' and ''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mino no Kuni Jinmyōki}}'', it appears as "Junior Fifth Rank Lower Grade, Tai Myōjin." It was also called "Tai-no-miya." In {{ill|Kanbun (era)|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228}} 5 ({{ill|1665|Q7582|qid=Q7582}}), a prohibition notice was issued by the local magistrate to protect the sacred precinct. Around {{ill|Tenpō|Q1369045|qid=Q1369045}} 10 ({{ill|1839|Q7616|qid=Q7616}}), shrine buildings deteriorated and rituals were interrupted; until around Meiji 5 ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}), it was barely maintained by residents of a neighboring village (Ōsugi Village). In Meiji 6 it was ranked as gōsha, and on March 27 of Meiji 40 it was designated a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=shinsen heihaku-ryō kyōshin jinja}}.

=== Shrine buildings ===
The current main sanctuary was rebuilt in Shōwa 47 ({{ill|1972|Q2476|qid=Q2476}}).
